This divergence in size likely reflects sex-specific selective pressures related to territory defense and sexual display. At the very beginning of life, hatchlings emerge from the egg at a remarkably modest wet weight of just 3.35 grams [Ww0 = 3.35 grams], representing only a tiny fraction of the adult mass they will eventually achieve. This altricial condition, where neonates are relatively underdeveloped and require intensive parental care, is typical of many passerines and sets the stage for a rapid period of growth and development that occurs within the nest environment.
